Furthermore, the fact that the patient has failed one restrictive procedure indicates that she will most likely fail Lap-Band.

A 19-year-old male enrollee has requested the prescription drug Lexapro for the treatment of his major depression. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the Health Plan’s criteria for coverage of the requested medication are medically appropriate and reasonable, and the patient has not met these criteria. In addition, the medical data contained in the record is rather limited. The treating physician does not explain his rationale for the current medications that are being used, nor does he explain what about the patient made him so “difficult to stabilize”. The treating physician suggests the patient “has become manic at times”, but he does not elaborate. Although the patient is now doing well, there is no s

Findings:  The physician reviewer found that this patient has been diagnosed with autism and a speech disorder.  Both of these are medically recognized and carry diagnostic codes.  As such, his medical problems are recognized and coded by the medical community.  Furthermore, the patient’s IQ falls into the very low normal range which would project him as capable of being educated.  Moreover, the patient’s speech therapy report indicates continued and steady improvement with his speech.  Each of these factors demonstrates that speech therapy is a medically appropriate inter

The mother of an eight-year-old male enrollee has requested an external insulin pump for him for the treatment of the enrollee’s diabetes. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that management of the enrollee's Type 1 Diabetes cannot be accomplished with insulin syringes.  The external insulin pump is able to provide insulin in 0.05 unit increments.  There is no alternative device available.  It is very important in children to avoid hypoglycemia, as they may not be able to recognize the symptoms of a decreasing blood glucose level.

A 61-year-old female enrollee has requested for a right total ankle replacement for treatment of her polyarticular arthritis.   Findings:  Three physician reviewers found that the results of a total ankle arthroplasty, as stated in the literature, do appear to be similar to those of an ankle fusion.  One must realize that this individual has had an attempted failed fusion already. The right total ankle arthroplasty, at this juncture, would be more beneficial than an attempted repeat fusion. An arthroplasty would allow some remaining motion and would be a reasonable option for this patient.

The parent of a five-year-old female enrollee has requested speech therapy for the treatment of the enrollee’s autism spectrum disorder and speech-language disorder. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the etiology of autism has not been clearly delineated, but the consensus is that it is a congenital disorder. The highlight of dysfunction in autism is a communication defect. Consistent speech therapy on a one-to-one basis is the only known method of improving communications in an autistic child.

A 35-year-old female enrollee has requested hospital services at a facility that can meet the immediate needs of her unborn child for the treatment of her high–risk pregnancy. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that this fetus has a significant congenital cardiac anomaly which will require intervention immediately after birth. A fetal echocardiogram is done prenatally to allow for the provider to plan the delivery at a tertiary center which can best deal with the defects and reduce mortality. Double outlet right ventricle (DORV) can have a mortality rate as high as 50% when combined with other cardiac anomalies. Transporting a sick newborn even for a short distance can add to that mortality rate. Additionally, it is n

A 61-year-old male enrollee has requested for Synvisc therapy for treatment of his osteoarthritis of the ankle.   Findings:  Three physician reviewers found that Synvisc injections have been approved for use in the knee, but there has been no documented approval for the use of Synvisc in the shoulder, elbow, hip, or ankle.  There is no documentation that viscosupplementation, such as Synvisc, is appropriate for post-traumatic arthritis of the ankle.  Although this patient has had treatment in the past, and it has been deemed to be helpful, it would not be medically appropriate to approve the viscosupplementation with Synvisc due to the fact that it has not been proven to be appropriate care for ankle arthrit

A 52-year-old female enrollee has requested for Synvisc injections for treatment of her knee pain.    Findings:  The physician reviewer found that there is no scientific evidence to support the medical necessity or effectiveness or safety of long-term Synvisc therapy.

A 54-year-old female enrollee has requested an osteochondral allograft for the treatment of her focal osteochondral lesion in the left knee.  Findings:  Two physician reviewers found that the patient is a 54-year-old female who seeks coverage for an osteochondral allograft of medial femoral condyle for suspected osteonecrosis. There is significant involvement of entire medial compartment of the knee. Allograft would not address involvement of medial tibial plateau. She is not an ideal candidate for an osteochondral allograft given her age and the tibial involvement. However, she is a good candidate for unicompartmental replacement.

A 60-year-old female enrollee has requested for MRI studies of the cervical spine and brain and MRA studies of the neck and brain for evaluation of her symptoms of visual and auditory disturbances and cognitive and mobility impairments. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that MRI of the brain and MRA of the brain and cervical arteries are standard of care in a patient with transient ischemic attack (TIA) symptoms, especially given the prolonged and atypical nature of the symptoms. The MRI of the brain and MRA of the neck and brain were medically appropriate and necessary. The MRI of the cervical spine was not medically necessary and was not appropriate because the patient’s symptoms did not suggest radicular or myelop

A 34-year-old male enrollee has requested for Lyrica 75mg for treatment of her degenerative disease of the lumbar spine. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that there is a lack of articles in the literature that support the use of Lyrica for pain associated with this patient’s condition. Its use here would be “off-label” and unproven.

The parent of a 16-year-old male enrollee has requested for growth hormone therapy for treatment of his short stature. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that Arimidex and growth hormone therapy was initiated in April 2007, and the initial three months growth response rose from a subnormal 2.4 cm per year to 12 cm per year. This supported a putative diagnosis of partial growth hormone deficiency or lack of physiological growth hormone secretion. No MRI of the brain appears to have been done, despite a history of chronic headaches.

An 84-year-old male enrollee has requested for an X-Stop procedure for treatment of his lumbar stenosis.   Findings:  Three physician reviewers found that there is no documentation in the medical literature that multiple level X-Stop procedures perform any better than standard traditional care for spinal stenosis. Additionally, there is the risk of component malalignment or slippage. There are no good long-term studies documenting the efficacy of this procedure in multilevel cases.

A 59-year-old female enrollee has requested physical therapy for the treatment of her back pain.  Findings:  The physician reviewer found that The patient is suffering from chronic symptoms with intermittent flare-ups.  She has had no neurological deficits on physical examination.  Additionally, she has had minimal pain at rest, with pain occurring primarily with activities such as walking, running, hiking and weight training. The additional physical therapy modalities utilized have little proven benefit in the medical literature.

A 44-year-old male enrollee has requested for long-term acute care for treatment of his herpes simplex 1 viral encephalitis. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that patient was medically stable, and he was able to go up and down stairs (20 steps) with the use of handrail. The patient was naming tasks with 55% accuracy, and he followed written directions with 100% accuracy.

A 63-year-old male enrollee has requested for CyberKnife radiosurgery for treatment of his prostate cancer. Findings:  Two physician reviewers found that a short course of high-fraction radiation treatments that will deliver the biological equivalent to 40 IMRT treatments is well advised considering the radiobiology of prostate cancer. Participation in the CyberKnife clinical trial for the treatment of prostate cancer would be considered optimal treatment according to NCCN guidelines.

A 51-year-old male enrollee has requested for an integrated weight change program for treatment of his morbid obesity. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that morbid obesity is widely recognized as a disease process with significant comorbidities. Treatment for this condition is clinically indicated and participation in the integrated weight change program is a reasonable alternative.

A 44-year-old male enrollee has requested for PET/CT scan for evaluation of his aggressive digital papillary adenocarcinoma.   Findings:  Three physician reviewers found that Lymphatic mapping and sentinel lymph node biopsy are useful in detecting early metastases. There is also one report of a pulmonary metastasis detected with CT. In this patient, PET/CT did identify a positive axillary node (twelve nodes biopsied, one was positive). PET/CT is useful in this patient’s tumor. An initial follow-up PET/CT should be approved at six months. Subsequent scan approval should be based on the clinical situation at the time.

The parent of a six-year-old female enrollee has requested  for emergency services  for treatment of the enrollee’s fever and vomiting.  Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the patient’s symptoms met prudent layperson criteria for emergency care. A prudent layperson parent with an average knowledge of medicine and a child with persistent vomiting and fever would reasonably expect the absence of emergency care to jeopardize the child’s health. These symptoms are very concerning in a small child because dehydration can occur quickly. Vomiting and fever alone may signify acute gastroenteritis, food poisoning, urinary tract infection, or respiratory tract infection (sinusitis, pharyngitis, pneumonia), to

A 38-year-old female enrollee has requested emergency services for the treatment of her head pain. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the patient complained of being unable to sleep due to a frontal headache. Two days earlier, she woke up with a bump on her head and a severe headache. The patient’s symptoms met prudent layperson criteria for emergency care. Although she had been evaluated by Plan providers two days earlier, there is evidence in the medical record that her headache pain worsened. A prudent layperson with an average knowledge of medicine, a history of previous hemorrhagic stroke and severe headache two days after being evaluated for head trauma, would reasonably expect the absence of emerge

A 34-year-old female enrollee has requested for “awake” brain tumor resection with brain mapping for treatment of her brain tumor.  Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the patient’s tumor was in a high-risk area and standard non-awake craniotomy would have been a dangerous procedure with little likelihood of a positive outcome in terms of functional and cognitive preservation. Appropriate surgical intervention required state-of-the-art technology and an experienced surgeon. Awake craniotomy was the right procedure and was performed without apparent harm to patient.

A 35-year-old female enrollee has requested for distal left greater saphenous vein ultrasound-guided transcatheter endovenous chemoablation (sclerotherapy) for treatment of her varicose veins. Findings:  Two physician reviewers found that the reflux at the saphenofemoral juncture was successfully treated by VNUS Closure as proven by the latest venous Doppler study. Ultrasound-guided sclerotherapy is a logical approach to removal of the residual small segment of distal left greater saphenous vein. The greater saphenous vein toward the ankle is of much smaller diameter, therefore wall approximation after sclerotherapy is more easily accomplished. A 39-year-old male enrollee has requested for the medication Enbrel for treatment of his  psoriasis.    Findings:  The physician reviewer found that this patient has psoriasis that is becoming aggressive and spreading in a short period of time.  He has only 20% BSA involvement to date, but his disease is active and increasing in distribution. He has failed several topical therapies and UVB phototherapy.  The patient most recently failed an adequate course of Soriatane.  Methotrexate is not a good option for this relatively young patient due to its long-term risks of hepatotoxicity.  Also, cyclosporin has multiple side effects and patients frequently flare when the medication is discontinued.  As the patient failed a trial of Sor

A 56-year-old female enrollee has requested for computed tomography angiography (CTA) of the coronary arteries for evaluation of her chest pain. Findings:  Two physician reviewers found that the patient has little cardiac risk and presents with atypical chest discomfort.  Although there were very mild non-diagnostic ECG changes on the stress test, the more accurate nuclear perfusion images were reported as entirely normal.  Therefore, the test should not be considered equivocal or non-diagnostic, but rather negative.  In this circumstance, no additional cardiac testing for coronary ischemia is medically necessary at this time.

A 54-year-old male enrollee has requested temperature gradient studies and surface electromyography for an evaluation of his back and leg pain. Findings:  Three physician reviewers found that temperature gradient studies and surface EMG are not recognized or generally accepted by the medical community as diagnostic technologies for this type of case. There are no objective studies demonstrating their effectiveness in evaluating this patient’s condition. The patient could have received an appropriate evaluation through standard tests and physical examination.

A 51-year-old female enrollee has requested Botox injections for the treatment of her pelvic pain. Findings:  Two physician reviewers found that while there is substantial interest in the use of Botox for various conditions, its efficacy in treating myofascial pelvic dysfunction has not been established. The use of Botox to paralyze pelvic floor muscles as a treatment for chronic symptoms is clearly still in the early stages of investigation. Until further studies document the safety and utility of this therapy, there is no clear clinical indication for the use of Botox in the treatment of persistent pelvic floor pain.

A 64-year-old female enrollee has requested  for Diovan HCT 160 mg for treatment of her hypertension. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that this patient has responded to higher doses of Diovan. While the patient did not respond to Diovan 80 mg, the requested higher dose of the medication has been effective in treating this patient’s hypertension. She has tried and failed Toprol XL. As long as the patient is responding to this medication, it should be continued.

The parent of a 15-year-old male has requested acute inpatient psychiatric services for treatment of the enrollee’s intermittent explosive disorder and attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).  Findings:  The physician reviewer found that at the time of admission, the patient was sleep-deprived and noted to be dysphoric and labile. He had no suicidal ideation, homicidal ideation, psychosis, hallucinations or medical issues. He did not require chemical or physical restraints. He was rude, disrespectful and did not follow rules during his hospital stay. However, he displayed no aggression or safety risk issues. He was given Vyvanse and Tripleptal. He participated well in family therapy. The clinical records do not suppor

A 61-year-old female has requested a QCT bone density study for the evaluation of osteoporosis.  Findings:  The physician reviewer found that DEXA scans can be less accurate in patients who are obese or who have a very small stature. A QCT bone density study is a volumetric study, and the study is not dependent on the patient’s body habitus. A QCT bone density is not affected by degenerative changes or surrounding calcifications. As this patient has small stature and has not tolerated several medications for osteoporosis, it was medically necessary to accurately determine the extent of her osteoporosis to determine the appropriate therapy. The QCT bone density scan was appropriate for this patient.

A 51-year-old female enrollee has requested a second opinion consultation with an out-of-network oncologist/surgeon for an evaluation of her for possible lymphoma. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that with the information provided, there is no medical necessity for the out-of-network evaluation as resources are available within the network for ongoing care of the patient. This patient needs the left axillary lymph node biopsied by a surgical excision (as noted in the pathology report, if continued clinical concern exists, an excisional biopsy would be warranted due to a potentially false negative result). These services can be provided within the network, and therefore, the requested consultation is not clinically indica

A 59-year-old male enrollee has requested Rituxan (rituximab) for the treatment of his cryoglobinemia. Findings:  Three physician reviewers found that cryoglobulinemia is relatively rare, and it is unlikely that a large, controlled clinical trial will be forthcoming anytime soon. For a patient such as this patient, treatment options include immunosuppressive therapy such as cyclophosphamide or cyclosporine, or rituximab. Rituximab is an attractive alternative as the potential risks are minimal and the results in small case series are promising. Treatment with rituximab may also improve renal function and abrogate the need for regular plasma exchanges.

The parent of an eight-month-old female has requested Synagis therapy for the treatment of RSV prophylaxis.  Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) guidelines recommend Synagis for RSV prophylaxis for premature infants born at 32 to 35 weeks gestation who are six months old or younger at the start of the RSV season if they possess two additional risk factors: school age siblings, day care attendance, airway abnormality, neuromuscular disease, or exposure to environmental air pollutants. There are, however, additional risk factors that not only increase the chance of morbidity, but also mortality in infants infected with RSV. The most striking of these is a birth weight less than

A 57-year-old female enrollee has requested hyperbaric oxygen treatment for the treatment of her soft tissue radiation necrosis of the brain. Findings:  Two physician reviewers found that although there is a theoretical risk of worsening a tumor with HBO and/or inducing seizures, there are numerous case studies and reports to show adjunctive benefit in reducing complications from late central nervous system (CNS) effects of radiation. Some conflicting reports indicate there may be no benefit. However, there is sufficient evidence to suggest this patient may benefit from HBO considering that her providers have weighed other first-line options.

A 53-year-old female enrollee has requested artificial disc replacement for treatment of her degenerative disk disease. Findings:  Three physician reviewers found that cervical artificial disc replacement has only recently been FDA approved and the procedure is of unproven efficacy. Long-term results are unknown and the long-term risks, viability, and complications are unclear. Though short-term results have been favorable, further studies and results are needed. Thus, the procedure cannot be recommended at this time.

A 52-year-old male enrollee has requested Benicar for the treatment of his hypertension. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that there is no objective clinical documentation to suggest a true allergy to an ACE inhibitor. Overall, Accupril is well-tolerated. Despite the patient’s vague complaints of side effects to two other medications, there is no clear reason from a medical perspective to not consider a formulary medication in this case.

A 50-year-old male enrollee has requested right hip resurfacing arthroplasty utilizing the Conserve Plus device for the treatment of his osteoarthritis of the right hip. Findings:  Two physician reviewers found that the enrollee is relatively young with a previously active lifestyle. The record documents that the patient has a low head/neck ratio and the Conserve Plus is the only device available in 2mm increments. The Conserve Plus hip resurfacing device is in clinical trial under FDA supervision and is classified as a category B1 device. Considering all of the clinical aspects, the Conserve Plus appears to be the most appropriate device for this patient.

A 50-year-old female enrollee has requested left knee osteochondral allograft for the treatment of her knee pain. Findings:  Two physician reviewers found that it is unclear from the record what conservative measures were rendered after the arthroscopic procedure. There is no documentation of formal physical therapy or the patient’s response to physical therapy. There is no indication that a cortisone injection was administered either diagnostically or as a potentially therapeutic modality. There is no apparent consideration of visco supplementation for early degenerative joint disease with well maintained joint spaces. The records do indicate the patient has lesions in the trochlear and the patellofemoral arti

A 59-year-old female has requested Lyrica for treatment of fibromyalgia and neuropathic pain.  Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the patient has had better control of pain with Lyrica.  In an Arthritis & Rheumatism 2005 article on the use of Lyrica for the treatment of fibromyalgia, there was a significant reduction in pain compared to placebo and improvements in fatigue. Lyrica has recently been FDA approved for the treatment of fibromyalgia. It is within standards of good medical practice to use Lyrica for chronic pain management. A dose of 75mg three times a day would be medically appropriate.

A 63-year-old male enrollee has requested a continuous glucose monitoring system (CGMS) and related supplies for the treatment of his type I diabetes. Findings:  Two physician reviewers found that there is no information provided documenting that the patient had a wide variability in his finger stick blood sugar results, frequent irreversible lows or significant complications prior to the use of the CGMS. In addition, it appears the patient’s diet may be a contributing factor to his reported poor control. There is no indication the patient has seen a dietician to evaluate his meal plan or eating patterns. As such, there is inadequate evidence to support this patient’s use of a CGMS.

A 59-year-old male enrollee has requested continued diabetes care management for the treatment of his diabetes. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the patient’s diabetes is under good control. At this point, he does not meet the criteria to enroll in the diabetes care program. Further involvement would not provide additional benefit. The patient should follow-up with his PCP and endocrinologist for further assistance if necessary.

A 26-year-old female enrollee has requested reimbursement for residential treatment services for treatment of chemical dependency.  Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the patient had no acute signs of withdrawal when she was admitted to the residential treatment facility and there were no serious medical, emotional or behavioral conditions that required 24-hour monitoring or supervision. Although she had a significant history of polysubstance abuse/dependence, there is no evidence she required on-going residential treatment. The patient could have been appropriately treated at a lower level of care such as chemical dependency program supervised by a psychiatrist.

A 35-year-old female has requested authorization the Minimed Paradigm Real Time continuing glucose monitoring system for treatment of diabetes.  Findings:  Three physician reviewers found that since their inception several years ago, continuous glucose monitoring systems have proven to be useful tools in finding unexpected hypo and hyperglycemia in insulin treated patients who are not in good control. Recent reports indicate that continuous glucose monitoring for up to three months results in improvement in A1c levels as well as in detecting unexpected hypo and hyperglycemia.

A 34-year-old female enrollee has requested for wedge resection or bisection of the ovaries (CPT 58920) for treatment of her polycystic ovaries. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that ovarian wedge resection or bisection of the ovaries is performed in the treatment of infertility, not for dysfunctional uterine bleeding. The submitted documentation does not include any documentation regarding the patient’s infertility from the time of her office visit in August 2004 until the date of surgery. If there is objective clinical evidence regarding the patient’s fertility issues, the patient’s request for reimbursement should be reconsidered.

A 57-year-old female enrollee has requested for 24 additional sessions of physical therapy (PT) for treatment of her thoracic outlet syndrome.  Findings:  The physician reviewer found that there is limited documentation of one-to-one skilled therapy. Details of the pool program including specific exercises or the number of repetitions completed is lacking. There is no objective documentation of functional progress in terms of activities of daily living. The patient could have reasonably transitioned to a home exercise program.

Findings:  Three physician reviewers found that there are several indications for MRI of the breast, which include a determination of the pre-operative extent of cancer, post-operative residual cancer, the extent of lobular cancer, the identification of an occult primary cancer with positive axillary lymph nodes, the screening of high risk patients, and problem solving. An indication for non-malignant disease is the evaluation of breast implants. Findings:  Two physician reviewers found that standard therapy for MCD is high dose prednisone, which clearly has long-term toxicities, some of which the patient is currently experiencing. If patients are steroid-dependent, a trial of Cytoxan is indicated. Once this fails, patients can be tried on cyclosporine or levamisole. CellCept is also gaining favor as a treatment in steroid-dependent glomerular diseases. Unfortunately, this patient has failed all of these therapies. A 46-year-old female enrollee has requested for Tysabri for treatment of her multiple sclerosis. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the FDA has approved Tysabri as monotherapy for the treatment of patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis to delay the accumulation of physical disability and reduce the frequency of clinical exacerbations. It is generally recommended for patients who have had an inadequate response to, or are unable to tolerate, alternate multiple sclerosis therapies.

The parent of a five-year-old male enrollee has requested speech therapy for the treatment of the enrollee’s articulation disorder and dysarthria. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that developmental delays including speech are common following prematurity, especially for those born at 25 weeks gestational age. The etiology of the language delay in prematurity is unclear. Individualized speech therapy is not generally considered clinically or medically indicated in this group of patients. The submitted documentation demonstrates that this patient’s deficits are educational in nature and do not warrant individualized private speech therapy.

A 56-year-old female has requested a repeat series of Hyalgan injections for the treatment of osteoarthritis.  Findings:  Two physician reviewers found that conservative treatment has not been effective for this patient. A repeat series of Hyalgan injections is the best treatment alternative at this time. This therapy can reasonably be expected to decrease her pain and postpone the need for surgical intervention.

A 45-year-old male enrollee has requested for the medication Lamisil for treatment of his onychomycosis.  Findings:  The physician reviewer found that there are other treatments and medications available that should resolve his asymptomatic infection.

The parent of a three-year-old female has requested speech therapy for treatment of apraxia and sensory integration dysfunction.  Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the diagnosis of childhood apraxia of speech is controversial, as is its etiology.  There are numerous theories as to the cause of childhood apraxia, but none are established in peer- reviewed journals. The medical necessity of speech and language therapy for childhood apraxia of speech has not been established.

The parent of a nine-year-old male enrollee has requested the medication Invega for the treatment of the enrollee’s Tourette Syndrome and Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the safety and efficacy of Invega in children and adolescents has not been studied nor established. Invega is not the standard of care for adult patients with either Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder or Tourette Syndrome.  The off label use of Invega for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder and/or Tourette Syndrome is at present considered investigational. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the benefit of consultation and treatment with an integrative medicine physician is not clear from the documents provided for review. The physician identified by the family does not list credentials that would qualify him to treat a child with a developmental disability or a child with an autistic spectrum disorder. A 65-year-old male enrollee has requested prescription medication Qualaquin for treatment of leg cramps.  Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the use of Qualaquin for the treatment of nocturnal leg cramps is not clinically appropriate nor is it   consistent with that definition. The FDA has specifically stated this drug should not be prescribed for leg cramps because of its side effects. The patient has documented heart disease and Qualaquin is known to have a significant impact on the conduction system within the heart. Additionally, there is very limited evidence of the effectiveness of this drug in preventing leg cramps in the peer-reviewed literature.

A 63-year-old male enrollee has requested Avastin, paclitaxel and carboplatin for the treatment of his malignant melanoma.  Findings:  Two physician reviewers found that an abstract presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology conference this year involved the use of carboplatin, paclitaxel and bevacizumab in 20 patients with metastatic melanoma. There was one partial response among all of the study participants. Although moderate effectiveness had been demonstrated with carboplatin and paclitaxel in the treatment of metastatic melanoma, there is no data indicating the addition of Avastin is useful. Thus, the proposed therapy offers no proven clinical advantage.

The parent of a 13-year-old male enrollee has requested Leukine for treatment of Crohn’s disease.  Findings:  The physician reviewer found that Leukine is designated for the treatment of neutropenia. Due to neutropenia the patient cannot be treated with either immunosuppressive agents such as 6-MP, Imuran or Remicade. As such, it is prudent and appropriate to use Leukine in this setting, which allows for treatment of the patient’s Crohn’s disease and neutropenia with a single agent.

The parent of a 17-year-old female enrollee has requested multiple outpatient therapy sessions for the treatment of the enrollee’s behavioral health problems. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the submitted clinical documentation demonstrates measurable improvement in the patient’s condition since she was admitted to inpatient treatment. The psychiatrist’s progress notes point to a steady improvement in the patient’s mood, perspective, and willingness to engage in treatment. Thereafter, all of the submitted documentation points to a similarly improved state, further supported by therapist’s notes, which regularly cite “attended session, she appeared happy and emotional.” Given the distinct absence of

The parent of a four-year-old male enrollee has requested  once weekly occupational therapy for the treatment of the enrollee’s autism. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that occupational therapy is often a useful adjunct to interventions for autism spectrum disorders. In this case, although the patient has high functioning autism he is deficient in fine and gross motor skills and sensory processing. His deficiencies are likely to improve with the proposed course of once weekly occupational therapy.

A 31-year-old male enrollee has requested re-treatment with Rituxan for treatment of rheumatoid arthritis.  Findings:  The physician reviewer found that Rituxan has received FDA approval for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis. Its effectiveness has been repeatedly demonstrated in trials involving various regimens including steroids, methotrexate, and cyclophosphamide, as well as in patients who previously failed TNF inhibitors.

A 71-year-old female enrollee has requested injectable methotrexate for treatment of her lupus anti-coagulant-type syndrome. Findings:  Three physician reviewers found that per the relevant literature, methotrexate is an appropriate treatment for undifferentiated connective tissue disease. The patient has achieved good results with methotrexate, but is unable to tolerate the oral form of the medication. Therefore, injectable methotrexate is clinically appropriate and indicated for this patient.

Findings:  The physician reviewer found that there are several indications for MRI of the breast which include evaluation of pre-operative extent of cancer, post-operative residual cancer, extent of lobular cancer, identification of an occult primary cancer with positive axillary lymph nodes, screening of high risk patients, and problem solving. An indication for non-malignant disease is evaluation of breast implants. High-risk patients are those with a personal or family history of breast cancer or a genetic predisposition for breast cancer such as a BRCA 1 or 2 gene. A 47-year-old female enrollee has requested  for acupuncture therapy for treatment of  her elbow and knee pain. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that acupuncture is a modality for the management of chronic pain. It is generally utilized to control or modulate chronic symptoms recalcitrant to more conservative or traditional evidence-based treatment approaches.A cortisone injection might also be considered. There is no evidence to suggest a chronic pain condition requiring acupuncture.

A 64-year-old male enrollee has requested surgical implantation of a bone anchored hearing aid (BAHA) for treatment of his hearing loss.   Findings:  The physician reviewer found that the BAHA is indicated for use in patients with hearing loss who cannot tolerate the use of a conventional amplification device. In the past, this was often interpreted to mean patients with external or middle ear disease that precluded the use of traditional hearing aids. Over the years, the use of this device has been expanded to include patients with severe unilateral sensorineural hearing loss. A 38-year-old female enrollee has requested for an out-of-network referral for surgical services for treatment her arteriovenous malformation. Findings:  The physician reviewer found that review of the medical literature regarding treatment of AVM includes a study in which operative intervention was directed at primary resection in 15 cases, stage resection in 7 cases, embolization and resection in 5 cases, and evacuation of hematoma in 3 cases. Operative mortality in this surgical series was 7%, with significant morbidity in 13% of patients.
